previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (LVEF 25%), ICD, chronic kidney disease, and a right humeral fracture was admitted for acute shortness of breath worsening when lying flat, consistent with fluid overload from heart failure exacerbation. Evaluation showed minimal pulmonary edema on chest X-ray, elevated BNP, and no acute ischemia. He was treated with IV furosemide and transitioned to increased oral torsemide. His diabetes was managed with insulin during admission due to elevated blood glucose, and he was restarted on glipizide at discharge. Insomnia and depression were addressed with continuation of imipramine and perphenazine, and initiation of mirtazapine. Subtherapeutic INR led to warfarin dose increase. He improved clinically, with resolution of pulmonary crackles and stable vital signs, and was discharged home with medication adjustments and follow-up plans.

Brief Hospital Course:
The patient is a ___ year old man with past medical history of 
non-ischemic  cardiomyopathy (EF 25%), NSVT s/p ICD, s/p AAA 
repair, PVD, HTN, CKD, who presented with with SOB.  
. 
ACTIVE MEDICAL PROBLEMS

# Acute on chronic CHF Exacerbation: 
The patient's history of progressive SOB preceded by recent 
increased salt intake, in addition to CXR revealing  
interstitial edema and elevated BNP were all consistent with a 
CHF exacerbation. He was given 100mg IV furosemide in the ED, 
with net ~1.5L output. Despite this, he continued to have SpO2 
in the low ___ on RA.
On the day of admission, he was diuresed further with an 
additional 20mg IV torsemide.  He diuresed a total of more than 
3L throughout his hospitalization and was symptomatically much 
improved, with ambulatory oxygen saturations above 93% prior to 
discharge. He remained hemodynamically stable throughout his 
hospital course, and was discharged on his home regimen of  
Spironolactone 12.5qd and Torsemide 20 po qd.
.
CHRONIC MEDICAL PROBLEMS

# Nonischemic cardiomyopathy with LV thrombus. 
The patient is currently anticoagulated with warfarin at a dose 
of 4mg daily. His INR was noted to be subtherapeutic at 1.4 on 
the day of discharge. He was given an extra dose of warfarin 4mg 
and instructed to obtain follow up labs at his next scheduled 
appointment. 
He was continued on his home dose of Amiodarone. 
.
#HTN
He was continued on home doses of metoprolol succinate, 
spironolactone, and torsemide.
.
# DIABETES, type 2, controlled: 
He was maintained on Humalog ISS while hospitalized, and home 
doses of oral medications were resumed at discharge.
.
# DEPRESSION: 
He was continued on outpatient regimen of perphenazine and 
imipramine.
.
# GERD:
He was continued on home dose of omeprazole 40 daily.

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES
-Follow up repeat INR
-Follow up with cardiology and PCP regarding further management 
of CHF and chronic medical problems.
